item.title: #3585933: Authorization denials surface as -32603 Internal server error, because the SDK dispatch loop swallows the exception
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585933 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Per-call authorization denials thrown from an SDK RequestEvent subscriber never produced a 401 or 403. The SDK's per-message guard turned them into an HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC -32603 Internal server error and an error-level log entry. The fix does not make that path work. It removes the handling that could never run and states the supported route: authorization belongs in a PSR-15 transport middleware, which answers a denial with its own 401 or 403 response before the SDK dispatches. Custom authorization code, and mcp_server_oauth 1.0.0-alpha1 (which still throws the exception), cannot deny calls this way. That code needs to move to middleware.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: McpServerController, McpExceptionSubscriber and the drush mcp:server command no longer catch or translate McpAuthorizationDeniedException; McpExceptionSubscriber drops its logger constructor argument.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\mcp_server\Exception\McpAuthorizationDeniedException is deprecated in mcp_server:2.0.0-beta6 and removed in 3.0.0.

Technical details

The exception is thrown inside Protocol::doProcessInput()'s catch (\Throwable) guard, so the controller catch and McpExceptionSubscriber could not be reached. Of the three options in the issue, the merged change picks neither out-of-band signalling nor an SDK change. It deletes the dead code and points to the existing mcp_server.transport_middleware tag, where a middleware returns its own PSR-7 response without entering SDK dispatch or the kernel exception path.

Removed: the McpAuthorizationDeniedException catch in McpServerController::handle(), the matching catch and JSON-RPC error writing in McpServerCommands, and the exception branch in McpExceptionSubscriber::onException(). That subscriber now only rewrites the route-level AccessDeniedHttpException (access mcp server) into -32001/-32002 with 401/403, and its @logger.channel.mcp_server argument was dropped from mcp_server.exception_subscriber in mcp_server.services.yml. The exception class stays, marked @deprecated, only because mcp_server_oauth 1.0.0-alpha1 still throws it.

The change adds a test fixture, StateArmedDenyingMiddleware in mcp_server_test, which denies tools/call with 401 or 403 when armed through State. It also adds TransportMiddlewareDenialTest, and the README authorization section and the .ai/kenkeep notes now describe the middleware route. The kenkeep note also records that on SDK releases with php-sdk#528 the throw would escape to core as a 500 rather than -32603, so throwing from a subscriber cannot deny a call either way.

Upgrade

Replace a RequestEvent subscriber that throws McpAuthorizationDeniedException with a PSR-15 middleware registered under the existing tag, which returns the denial itself:

services:
  mcp_server_test.middleware.denying:
    class: Drupal\mcp_server_test\Middleware\StateArmedDenyingMiddleware
    tags:
      - { name: mcp_server.transport_middleware, priority: 50 }

In process(), return a PSR-7 response with status 401 or 403, JSON-RPC error code -32001 or -32002, and a WWW-Authenticate header, instead of calling $handler->handle($request). The test fixture StateArmedDenyingMiddleware shows the full pattern.

item.title: #3518120: Define tools with attributes on typed methods
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3518120 · 4 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

The Tool API module can now turn a public method of an existing service into a tool by adding PHP attributes, with no plugin class. The method's parameters become the tool's inputs, its return value becomes the output, and the docblock supplies the descriptions. Access is never inferred. Each tool must declare a permission, an access method, or an entity operation on each entity parameter. Existing #[Tool] plugins can also declare a typed __invoke() and get the same inference, so they can be converted one definition at a time. This landed in the 1.0.x-dev release.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolBase::doExecute() is no longer abstract: a #[Tool] plugin may declare a typed __invoke() instead. Other changes to existing behavior are listed in the MR.
  • New API: New attributes ToolMethod, ToolInput, ToolEntityInput, ToolOutput and ToolProperty in Drupal\tool\Attribute, plus Drupal\tool\Tool\Method\MethodTool as the plugin class for method tools.

Technical details

#[ToolMethod] goes on a public service method, or on the class of an invokable service, where it applies to __invoke(). It requires an explicit id, because agent, ECA and MCP configuration refer to tools by ID. operation defaults to ToolOperation::Write. Access options are permission (same syntax as #[Tool]) and access (a service method returning an AccessResultInterface). Every entity parameter must use #[ToolEntityInput(op: ...)], which is checked through the entity's access handler. A method with no declared check fails discovery. An entity operation only counts if it sits on a required, single entity parameter.\n\n#[ToolInput] refines a parameter. #[ToolOutput] names or refines the output, and two or more declare several outputs. An array{...} shape in @return also declares several outputs. #[ToolProperty] marks the public properties or zero-argument methods of a plain PHP value object to publish. Outputs can narrow to a subset with members:.\n\nInference reads native and docblock types: scalars, entities, backed enums, DateTime, lists, and array{} shapes. Unsupported parameter types fail discovery.\n\nDiscovery runs in a compiler pass that scans service class sources for the attribute name before autoloading them. It records the results in the tool.method_tools container parameter, which the tool manager merges with plugin discovery. A definition that cannot be built is logged to the tool channel and skipped. The other tools still load. Definitions are cached, so a new attribute needs a cache rebuild.\n\nA method may return an ExecutableResult to set its own message, failure category, or outputs on failure. Throwing Drupal\\tool\\Exception\\InputException reports a caller error. Other exceptions are logged and the caller only learns that the run failed. For #[Tool] plugins, a typed __invoke() is used when doExecute() is not overridden, and a plugin that declares #[ToolEntityInput] parameters but overrides access() is skipped at discovery. The change also adds a docs page, docs/developers/tool-methods.md, and a Typed tools section in the creating-a-tool docs.

Upgrade

To convert an existing #[Tool] plugin, replace doExecute() and the input_definitions/output_definitions arrays with a typed __invoke():\n\nphp\n#[ToolOutput(name: 'message')]\npublic function __invoke(string $name, ?string $greeting = NULL): string {\n return ($greeting ?? 'Hello') . \", $name!\";\n}\n\n\nThe required op on #[ToolEntityInput] adds an access check on every entity passed in, so a converted tool can deny calls the old plugin allowed. Throw InputException instead of \\InvalidArgumentException for messages meant for the caller.

item.title: #3583049: Deprecate `multiple` on input and output definitions in favor of list definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583049 · 1 contributor · 11 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Declaring a tool input or output as multiple: TRUE is now deprecated in favor of declaring a list definition. Existing multiple declarations still load: they are converted to a list automatically and trigger a deprecation notice. The advertised JSON Schema stays the same. The conversion also fixes a bug where a Count constraint on a multiple input rejected every value, because Count now applies to the list and not to each item. The multiple option is planned for removal in 1.0.0-rc1.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The $multiple constructor parameter is dropped from ListInputDefinition and ListOutputDefinition, so positional arguments after $required shift by one.
  • Deprecation: multiple: TRUE on input definitions, output definitions (including core ContextDefinition passed as outputs), map properties and refiner results is deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta10 and removed in 1.0.0-rc1; declare list definitions instead.

Technical details

The two ways of declaring a list disagreed about where constraints go. A multiple input copied every constraint, Count included, onto each item, so Count failed every value. The new ListInputDefinition::fromMultiple() splits the constraints: those that describe the list, such as Count, go on the list, and the remaining constraints stay on a required item copy with no label or description. This is the same split the normalizer already applies to the JSON Schema, so the output is unchanged. The one exception is the default value, which moves to the list and is no longer advertised on each item. Both ListInputDefinition and ListOutputDefinition have a fromMultiple(). It is marked @internal and is deleted together with multiple.\n\nThe conversion happens at several entry points, each with an E_USER_DEPRECATED pointing at work item 3583049. ToolDefinition::addInputDefinition() converts inputs. MapDefinitionBase converts map properties, to either an input or an output list. OutputDefinition::fromContextDefinition() turns a core ContextDefinition with multiple into a ListOutputDefinition. TypedInputsTrait converts a refiner result that returns multiple: TRUE, before the narrowing check runs. Lists produced by conversion are flagged (isConvertedFromMultiple() in ListDefinitionBase) so the refiner constraint split and the entity handle transformer treat them correctly. Bundled test tools such as ComprehensiveTypesTool and SchemaMatrixTool were moved to explicit list definitions, and docs/developers/input-output-definitions.md was updated.\n\nStep 2 of the issue, removing isMultiple()/setMultiple() and the $multiple constructor parameters, is not part of this change.

Upgrade

Replace multiple: TRUE with a list definition, as in the issue's example. Put list-level constraints such as Count on the list and per-item constraints on the item:

$list = new ListInputDefinition(
  label: 'Tags',
  description: 'Tags.',
  constraints: ['Count' => ['min' => 2]],
  item_definition: new InputDefinition(
    data_type: 'string',
    label: 'Tag',
    description: 'A tag.',
    constraints: ['Length' => ['min' => 3]],
  ),
);

Anything that constructs ListInputDefinition or ListOutputDefinition with positional arguments must drop the old $multiple argument. The new signature is ($label, $description, $required, $default_value, $constraints, $item_definition, ...). Using named arguments avoids the problem.

item.title: #3583078: Decide before rc1: separate invocation state from the tool definition behind one execution path
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583078 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Tool module now has one place that runs a tool call: the tool.runner service. It checks the declared permission, sets inputs, validates, checks access and executes, in that order, so each caller no longer repeats the sequence. The tool:run Drush command and the AI connector now use it. Failure messages changed as a result: for example Access denied for tool send_email. The 'send emails' permission is required. and Invalid input: followed by the violations. Anyone parsing the old wording needs to adjust. The runner also gives a place to attach future features such as destructive-tool confirmation, at-most-once execution and auditing, but none of those are implemented here. This landed as a first phase: the plugin is still stateful and the invocation object is only a view over the tool instance. The issue's comments, which hold the agreed plan, could not be retrieved, so the summary is based on the merged commit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New tool.runner service (Drupal\tool\Tool\ToolRunner::run()) returning a Drupal\tool\Tool\ToolInvocation; drupal:user added as a dependency of the Tool module.

Technical details

ToolRunner::run($tool_id, $values, $configuration, $invoker, $account) first runs ToolManager::checkPermission() against the definition, before any plugin instance exists. It then switches to an explicit $account with the account switcher and restores it in a finally block. A blocked non-anonymous UserInterface account is refused with an Access failure. Inside the switch it creates the instance, calls setInputValue() for each value, then validateInputs(), access() and execute(), and finally materializes getFormattedResult() so output transforms (handle downcasting) run at execute time. InputException and HandleExceptionInterface are caught and recorded as FailureCategory::Input. Validation and access denials are written to the tool with setFailureResult(). Comments in the code mark where an at-most-once claim, destructive confirmation and auditing would attach.\n\nrun() always returns a ToolInvocation, whether the call was denied or completed. It exposes getResult(), getFormattedResult(), getInputValue(), getInputDefinitions(), getTool() and hasExecuted(). getTool() is NULL when the call was denied before the tool was instantiated. The class docblock says the per-call state is intended to move into the invocation later.\n\nToolRunCommand no longer switches accounts itself. It passes account: to the runner and maps the invocation to output: refusals before execute become RunErrorType::AccessDenied or InvalidInput, and an exception escaping the runner becomes ExecutionFailed. In tool_ai_connector, ToolPluginBase collects the declared inputs, calls the runner with ToolAiConnectorInvoker::create(), adopts the executed instance as its toolPluginInstance, and mirrors the transformed inputs into its contexts. The Explorer execute form is not changed in this commit. The developer docs now recommend tool.runner and describe the manual sequence for invokers such as the Explorer form that drive the stages themselves.

Upgrade

Invokers can replace the hand-written sequence with the runner:

$invocation = \Drupal::service('tool.runner')
  ->run('my_tool', values: ['name' => 'value']);
$result = $invocation->getResult();

Pass account: to run as a specific account. Code or tests matching the old messages (Tool plugin access denied, Tool plugin execution failed, Input validation failed for tool ...) should match Access denied for tool <id>. and Invalid input instead.

item.title: #3583085: Tell callers which input a failed tool call is about
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583085 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

When a tool call fails on bad input, the failed result now says which input was at fault, as data rather than only inside the message text. A client such as an MCP agent can read the input name and pass it back to the model for a retry. A tool that checks several inputs together, such as an end date that must follow a start date, can now name the input it is complaining about. Failure messages are reworded to show each problem as input_name: reason, with the duplicate naming removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: InputException now extends \InvalidArgumentException, and getExecutableValues()/getExecutableValue()/setConfigurationValue() throw it (with violations) instead of a bare \InvalidArgumentException. ToolResultInterface gains a method, and ToolInterface::setFailureResult() gains an optional third $violations parameter. Failure message text changed: the Input @name: and The @label input is invalid: wrappers are gone, replaced by a name: reason line prefix, and Tool execution failed due to invalid input: became Invalid input:.
  • New API: ToolResultInterface::getViolations() on results, InputException::getViolations(), getInputNames(), fromViolations(), and an inputNames constructor argument; ToolMessages::invalidInput() added.

Technical details

validateInputValues() in TypedInputsTrait now keeps each violation's message as the reason alone and sets its property path to the input's machine name, joined to any inner path via the new ValueViolationsTrait::joinPath() (for example product.sku). The per-violation wrappers Input @name: and The @label input is invalid: are removed, and several other messages dropped their label (This input is locked..., This property is required., This input must be an entity.). ToolMessages::violationList() now prefixes each line with its path, so text output reads recipient: This value should not be null.. A new ToolMessages::invalidInput() supplies the single Invalid input: message template used by ToolRunner, and ToolBase::execute().

InputException now takes a named inputNames argument (new InputException($message, inputNames: ['end_date']); the issue text called it inputs, but the merged code uses inputNames). Each name becomes a violation with the reason as message and the name as path. InputException::fromViolations() wraps validation violations, and getViolations() and getInputNames() read them back. MarkupInterface messages are converted to plain text once in the constructor. ExecutableResult::failure() and the constructor accept an optional violation list, exposed by the new getViolations() on ToolResultInterface (also forwarded by FormattedExecutableResult). It is empty for a success or a failure without violations. ToolBase::execute() catches InputException separately and fills the result's violations from it. A bare \InvalidArgumentException thrown by tool code still fails as input, with message Invalid input: @message and no violations. List item and map property positions still appear in the message text rather than on the path; that is left to #3583065.

Upgrade

Tools that validate across inputs should name the input when throwing:

throw new InputException(new TranslatableMarkup('The end date must be after the start date.'), inputNames: ['end_date']);

Pass TranslatableMarkup objects directly, not cast to string. Code or tests that match on the old text (Input recipient: ..., The X input is invalid: ..., Tool execution failed due to invalid input: ...) should read the input from $result->getViolations() (getPropertyPath()) or expect the new name: reason lines under Invalid input:. Any custom ToolResultInterface implementation must add getViolations(), and any ToolInterface::setFailureResult() override must accept the new optional ?ConstraintViolationListInterface $violations = NULL parameter.

Contribution

item.title: #3588987: Add Config Split guidance to the drupal-configuration skill
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3588987 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

The drupal-configuration skill in AI Best Practices now covers Config Split, which it previously never mentioned. Its decision table gains a row for config or modules that should vary by environment, and a new reference explains how to choose between complete and partial splits, when to use a split instead of a settings.php override, and how to set one up. It also warns about a common export mistake that can remove required config such as system.site from config/sync/. AI agents using the skill will give better environment-specific config advice.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

skills/drupal-configuration/SKILL.md adds a "Config Split" row to the decision table, a paragraph telling the agent to read references/config-split.md first, and a See also link. The new reference file explains:

  • Complete vs. partial splits. Complete splits remove the listed config or module from config/sync/. Partial splits keep it there and store only a config_split.patch.<config name>.yml diff.
  • Split vs. override. A $config override in settings.php suits a single value or a secret, since it is never exported. A partial split suits structural or multi-key differences that should be shared with the team.
  • Setup. The split folder goes outside the sync directory. The split is saved with status off, then enabled per environment with $config['config_split.config_split.dev']['status'] = TRUE; in settings.php.
  • Export trap. If a partial-split item is not already in config/sync/, drush cex moves it entirely into the split. Other environments then lose it on import. The fix is to export once with the split off first.

The commit also adds static checks in evals/drupal-configuration/static-checks.json and updates the eval README for this content. The reference states it matches Config Split 2.x.

item.title: #3583094: A required input explicitly set to NULL throws ContextException from execute() and access()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583094 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

A required input with no default that was explicitly set to NULL used to crash when code called a tool's execute() or access() directly. execute() reported an unhelpful runtime failure, and access() threw a ContextException. Both now behave the way validateInputs() already did. execute() returns an input failure naming the input. access() returns Forbidden with the reason Tool input validation failed. Callers that go through ToolRunner or the MCP bridge were not affected, because those call validateInputs() first.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The cause was that validateInputs() had its own explicit-NULL rule, but getExecutableValues() resolved values through getExecutableValue(). For a required input with no default, that call threw ContextException from the default-value path. The issue itself was closed with no separate merge request. The fix landed as a side effect of the commit for #3583085. That commit moves the rule into a shared resolveInputValues() in TypedInputsTrait. In that method, an input or configuration value explicitly set to NULL, on an unlocked, required definition with no default, resolves to NULL so it can be reported as a violation. getExecutableValues() calls it and then validates, throwing the violations as InputException::fromViolations(). validateInputs() reads the same values through getExecutableValues(TRUE), so a subclass override of that accessor applies to validation and execution alike. execute() and access() already handled InputException as an input problem. ToolBaseTest::testExplicitNullRequiredInputIsAnInputFailure() covers both paths using numeric_input_tool.

Contribution

item.title: #3585928: Session lock delays elicitation and sampling replies until the lease expires
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585928 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

Tools that ask the client for something mid-call, through ClientGateway::elicit(), sample() or listRoots(), no longer stall for about 30 seconds per round trip. The session lock added in #3585923 had been holding off the client's reply until the lock lease expired. The reply is now accepted while the streamed response is waiting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The module now uses an @internal subclass, SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport, in place of the SDK's StreamableHttpTransport. The issue picked the "release the lock while waiting" option. Letting reply-only POSTs skip the lock was rejected because the SDK saves the session as one blob, so an unlocked write could clobber the stream's _mcp.outgoing_queue (upstream php-sdk#275).

In McpServerController::handle(), the streaming callback now calls lockSessionPerWrite() on the transport and then releases the request-wide session lock. From then on the transport takes the lock only around the session read-modify-writes in the SDK's streaming loop, by overriding getOutgoingMessages(), checkForResponse() and handleFiberYield(). The client's reply POST can therefore get in between polls. If the lock cannot be acquired after one wait(), it throws LockAcquiringException.

If a database transaction is open (Connection::inTransaction()) when the stream starts, the controller keeps holding the lock for the whole stream. A rollback would undo the release. The subclass overrides protected SDK hooks, which the class docblock says can change in any mcp/sdk minor release. The controller now also takes the database service. The commit adds an ElicitingTool test plugin and extends McpServerFunctionalTest to cover an elicitation round trip.

Contribution

Timeline

item.title: #3585939: mcp/sdk 0.8 logs an empty middleware list warning on every HTTP request
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585939 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

With mcp/sdk 0.8, every MCP HTTP request wrote a warning to the site log saying the Streamable HTTP transport started with an empty middleware list. The warning is gone. CORS handling stays with Drupal's cors.config, and Host validation stays with trusted_host_patterns. The SDK's own CORS and DNS-rebinding middleware remain off, so there are still no duplicate CORS headers and no 403 for non-localhost hosts.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The SDK warns only when the middleware list is exactly []. It installs its default CORS and DNS-rebinding middleware only when it gets null. McpServerController::handle() now uses $this->middlewareCollector->getMiddleware() ?: [new PassThroughMiddleware()]. When no module tags a mcp_server.transport_middleware service, the transport gets a one-entry list holding a no-op middleware. If any middleware is tagged, the controller passes that stack unchanged. The issue text proposed tagging the pass-through as a service. The merged diff instead instantiates it in the controller, so there is no new service definition.

Drupal\mcp_server\Transport\PassThroughMiddleware is a final, @internal PSR-15 middleware that calls $handler->handle($request). Its docblock says mcp/sdk 0.9 ships its own PassthroughMiddleware, which can replace it once 0.9 is the minimum. The SDK maintainers suggested this opt-out in php-sdk#523, instead of a constructor flag. A logger wrapper that matched on the SDK's message text was dropped, because that text can change in any SDK minor. A kernel test in McpServerControllerTest asserts that an initialize request returns 200 and logs no record containing "empty middleware list". The diff also updates the project's internal knowledge-base docs. Those docs say ProtocolVersionMiddleware only applies on mcp/sdk 0.7 and that McpServerServiceProvider::alter() removes it on 0.8. That change is not part of this MR's code diff.

item.title: #3583051: ListInputDefinition and MapInputDefinition accept output definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583051 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

List and map input definitions in the Tool module now reject output definitions. Before, passing an output definition as a list input's item or as a map input's property was accepted and then silently ignored. Now it throws an \InvalidArgumentException, matching what the output definitions already do for input definitions.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Since #3583019 the shared base methods ListDefinitionBase::setItemDefinition() and MapDefinitionBase::setPropertyDefinitions() accept any input or output definition. Only the output classes narrowed that. ListInputDefinition::setItemDefinition() and MapInputDefinition::setPropertyDefinitions() now override the base methods. They check for InputDefinitionInterface and throw \InvalidArgumentException otherwise, then delegate to the parent. Without the check, ListInputDefinition::getItemDefinition() fell back to an untyped any input item, so the declared output item was dropped. The issue says the map input walker skips output-definition properties. Unit tests mirroring the output-side boundary tests were added; this was not checked against a diff, since none was provided. The issue states there are no advertised schema changes.

item.title: #3583063: Reject the generic entity data type in the entity definition family
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583063 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Declaring a tool input or output with new EntityInputDefinition('entity') or new EntityOutputDefinition('entity') now throws an InvalidArgumentException immediately. Previously it silently produced the nonexistent entity:entity type, and the error only appeared later, for example when the tool's input schema was generated. The message tells authors to use a plain InputDefinition or OutputDefinition with data type entity for a generic "any entity" declaration.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EntityDefinitionBase::normalizeEntityDataType() prefixes any value lacking entity:. It now throws when the value is exactly entity. EntityInputDefinition and EntityOutputDefinition both construct through this helper, so the one guard covers both. Only the exact string entity is rejected; node and entity:node behave as before. The issue argues the guard cannot break a working declaration, because entity:entity already failed downstream with PluginNotFoundException. A unit test, EntityDefinitionGenericTypeTest, was added. The behavior mirrors core's EntityContextDefinition, which has the same shorthand and the same trap. The issue notes that tool_belt hit this with a generic entity list item.

Upgrade

If you declare a generic entity with the entity definition classes, switch to the base definitions:

// Before: now throws InvalidArgumentException.
new EntityInputDefinition('entity');
// After: use a plain InputDefinition (or OutputDefinition) of type 'entity'.

Contribution

Timeline

item.title: #3583076: Let a string definition say what it contains with contentMediaType
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583076 · 1 contributor · 8 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Tool input and output definitions can now say what a string holds, such as plain text, HTML or Markdown. Before, a title and an HTML caption produced the same schema, so a front end or a model had to guess from the description which one was markup. Adding a MediaType constraint with a type such as text/html now makes the generated schema carry a contentMediaType entry. Existing definitions and schemas are unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New MediaType validation constraint (plugin ID MediaType, option type) that the normalizer emits as JSON Schema contentMediaType.

Technical details

MediaTypeConstraint is registered with the #[Constraint] attribute under the ID MediaType and requires a non-empty string type option. It throws MissingOptionsException otherwise. Its validator, MediaTypeConstraintValidator, accepts every value. This follows JSON Schema, where contentMediaType is descriptive and not an assertion. The constraint is used because the constraints array is where a definition already carries facts beyond its type, and the normalizer already reads Email and Uuid from there to emit format. In ContextDefinitionNormalizer, when MediaType is present and the schema type is string, the type option is emitted as contentMediaType. The constructor accepts either named arguments or a single options array, so it works on cores with and without named-argument support (Drupal 10). The docblock says the constraint does not make markup safe: consumers must still filter text/html values. The issue says it was extracted from #3518120, where media_type: on attribute-defined tool attributes builds on it. Docs were updated in docs/developers/input-output-definitions.md, and tests were added.

Upgrade

'caption' => new OutputDefinition(
  data_type: 'string',
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('Caption'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('The image caption.'),
  constraints: ['MediaType' => ['type' => 'text/html']],
),
// {"type": "string", "contentMediaType": "text/html", ...}

item.title: #3585937: Tool call arguments and results end up in the Drupal log
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585937 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

MCP Server no longer writes tool call arguments and results to the Drupal log by default. Before, one tools/call could leave the full request and the tool result in Database Logging, readable by anyone with access site reports. The log now shows the JSON-RPC method and the outcome. Sites that want full payloads while debugging can turn them back on with a container parameter.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Tool arguments, results and request payloads no longer land in dblog or other log backends by default, where anyone with access site reports could read them.
  • Config change: New mcp_server.log_payloads container parameter, false by default, set in services.yml rather than config.

Technical details

The fix is in McpContextLogger, the PSR-3 decorator that appends @mcp_* placeholders so context values survive into dblog. It now takes a second constructor argument, bool $logPayloads (default FALSE), wired in mcp_server.services.yml from the new mcp_server.log_payloads parameter (default false).

When payloads are off, a private withoutPayload() filters each context value. An object implementing HasMethodInterface is reduced to its method. A Response or JSON-RPC Error is reduced to its ID. The SDK's raw input under the message key is dropped, and so is any array or non-stringable object. Dropping is by type and not by a list of key names, so a payload logged under a new SDK key stays out too. Throwable, Stringable and UnitEnum values and scalars are kept, and the existing exception handling is unchanged. Dropped keys are also removed from the context passed to the inner logger, because backends such as Monolog can store the whole context and not just the placeholders in the message.

The switch is a container parameter and not config, so it is set in development.services.yml and cannot reach production through config sync. The README documents it.

Upgrade

To log tool arguments and results in full while debugging, set the parameter in a services file such as development.services.yml:

parameters:
  mcp_server.log_payloads: true

item.title: #3585940: The answer to an elicitation waits 30 seconds for the session lock over HTTP
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585940 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Sites running the MCP Server module's HTTP transport could see a tool that asks the connecting AI client a question (via elicitation) take 30 seconds longer than necessary to resume, even when the client answered within a couple of seconds. The delay came from an internal session lock, not from the client or network, so nothing a site owner configured could work around it. The fix removes this artificial wait so elicitation answers are picked up as soon as they arrive.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

McpServerController::handle() takes a mcp_session:-prefixed lock for the duration of the request and, for streamed (SSE) responses, only releases it once the stream ends, as established by the earlier fix for #3585923. When a tool calls ClientGateway::elicit(), the SDK suspends the handler's fiber and keeps that first request's SSE connection open while it polls the session store for the client's reply, which arrives as a second POST on the same Mcp-Session-Id. That second request calls into LockBackendInterface::wait() and blocks until the first request's lock lease expires, 30 seconds by default, so an answer submitted in two seconds is not read until the 30 second mark, and once the lease does expire both requests can end up writing the session at the same time.

The issue lays out two candidate fixes: skip acquiring the lock at all for a POST whose body contains only JSON-RPC responses (as opposed to a request that can itself trigger new elicitation), or release the lock while the handling fiber is suspended waiting on an elicitation answer and reacquire it when the handler resumes. No merge request or commit was available to confirm which approach was ultimately implemented, so the end-state mechanics above reflect the proposed resolution from the issue rather than a verified diff.

item.title: #3585936: ProtocolVersionMiddleware registered as a custom transport middleware rejects clients on protocol 2026-07-28
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585936 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

On mcp_server 2.x with mcp/sdk 0.8 or later, any MCP client request carrying the MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28 header was rejected with HTTP 400 (error -32022 Unsupported protocol version), and a client that only speaks that era could not connect to the server at all. The SDK also logged a warning on every single HTTP request complaining about the module's middleware setup. This is fixed: clients using the 2026-07-28 protocol era now connect and work normally, and the spurious warnings are gone. Sites still running mcp/sdk 0.7 are unaffected and keep the previous behavior.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was that mcp_server.services.yml registered the SDK's ProtocolVersionMiddleware as a custom transport middleware (mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version), running at the edge of every request before the SDK's transport had decided which protocol era the request belonged to. That made sense on mcp/sdk 0.7, which validates the header itself nowhere else, but from mcp/sdk 0.8 StreamableHttpTransport applies the same check internally, scoped to handshake-era requests only, so the module's copy became redundant and, because it runs unconditionally, actively rejected the newer era it didn't know about.

The fix removes the service dynamically rather than editing the static YAML: McpServerServiceProvider::alter() now checks method_exists(StreamableHttpTransport::class, 'handshakeMiddleware') and, when true (sdk >= 0.8), calls $container->removeDefinition('mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version'). This keeps a single codebase working across both the 0.7 and 0.8 SDK generations: on 0.7 the custom middleware stays registered and still guards the handshake; on 0.8+ the SDK's own handshake-scoped check takes over. Coverage was added in ProtocolVersionTest (a 2026-07-28 request now reaches the SDK and is served, while an unknown version header still gets -32022), and TransportMiddlewareCollectorTest was updated to assert the middleware list is empty of ProtocolVersionMiddleware on sdk 0.8+.

item.description:

Summary

The MCP Server module's tool administration UI is being reworked: instead of manually creating a config entity for every tool you want to expose, all discovered Tool plugins and their individual tools are listed automatically under Configuration > Services > MCP Server > Tools. Admins browse plugins, open a plugin's tool list, and simply check "Enabled" per tool (optionally overriding its exposed name/description and setting per-tool authentication/OAuth scopes); the underlying configuration entity is created, updated, or removed for you on save. The separate "Add tool" form and its autocomplete lookup are gone. Alongside the UI change, the MR also migrates three concrete Tool plugins onto this plugin-based system: a general site-info tool, a content search tool, and a Drush-command-runner tool, all previously part of the older mcp module.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The entity.mcp_tool_config.add_form, edit_form, delete_form routes and the mcp_server.tool_autocomplete route/controller are removed; tool management now goes through the new mcp_server.tool_plugins and mcp_server.plugin_tools routes.

Technical details

The old entity-form based workflow (McpToolConfigForm with add/edit/delete routes plus ToolAutocompleteController for picking a plugin_id:tool_name) is replaced by ToolPluginListController::list(), which renders a table of every ToolPluginManager::getDefinitions() entry with an "N of M enabled" count and a link into mcp_server.plugin_tools. That route is backed by PluginToolsForm, which lays out every tool from one plugin in vertical tabs: an enabled checkbox, an editable MCP name (validated for global uniqueness across plugins), a custom description, authentication_mode (required/optional/disabled), and OAuth scopes. PluginToolsForm::submitForm() creates or updates the matching McpToolConfig entity (machine id generated via generateUniqueMachineId()) when a tool is enabled, or deletes it when disabled, so the config entity's structure and storage are unchanged (per the issue, "data model changes: none"); only how entities get created changes. McpToolConfig's annotation drops its form handlers and links block accordingly, and mcp_server.links.task.yml/links.action.yml point the "Tools" local task at the new mcp_server.tool_plugins route instead of the entity collection.

The MR also adds three #[Tool]-attributed plugins under src/Plugin/Tool/: General, Content (a search_content tool that builds a node entity query from arbitrary field filters/operators, enforcing accessCheck(TRUE) and restricting filterable/returned fields via isSupportedField()), and DrushCaller (discovers available Drush commands via drush list --format=json and executes them through Symfony Process, building each command's inputSchema from Drush's own argument/option metadata). These are plugins only; a tool is still not exposed over MCP until an admin explicitly enables it through the new UI, which also governs its authentication mode and scopes. A new mcp_server/admin library/CSS file supplies the table, pill, and badge styling used by both the plugin list and per-plugin tool forms.

Upgrade

item.title: #3585884: Version requirements in submodule .info files causes issues
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585884 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Installing MCP Server from an unreleased dev snapshot via Composer left the main mcp_server.info.yml without version metadata (Drupal only stamps a module's version when drupal.org tags a release). A prior change had added a mcp_server:mcp_server (>=2.0) version constraint to the submodules' dependency declarations, so Drupal could not resolve that constraint against the versionless parent module. This blocked enabling the submodules (UI, OAuth, tool bridge, examples) from the admin interface and made drush core:requirements report unresolved dependency errors, breaking CI/CD pipelines that check requirements. The fix removes the problem at its root: the affected submodules are no longer shipped inside the mcp_server project at all. They have been split out into separate companion projects with their own Composer-managed versioning, so the in-tree version constraint that caused the failure no longer exists.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The constraint was introduced in commit a82ea733 (issue #3585873), which added mcp_server:mcp_server (>=2.0) to the dependencies key of mcp_server_ui.info.yml, mcp_server_oauth.info.yml, mcp_server_tool_bridge.info.yml, and mcp_server_examples.info.yml. Since dev installs of mcp_server carry no version string, Drupal's dependency resolver treats >=2.0 as unsatisfiable and refuses to enable the dependents, both in the admin UI and via drush core:requirements.

The actual fix landed in #3585898 ("Extract in-tree submodules into separate companion projects"), which deletes modules/mcp_server_ui, modules/mcp_server_oauth, modules/mcp_server_tool_bridge, and modules/mcp_server_examples from this repository along with their require-dev entries (drupal/simple_oauth, e0ipso/simple_oauth_21) in composer.json. Core mcp_server is now a standalone module with no Drupal module dependencies, requiring only php and mcp/sdk at the Composer level, which removes the problematic info.yml version constraint entirely rather than trying to work around it.

item.title: #3585885: Surface MCP InitializeResult.instructions via mcp_server.settings
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585885 · 1 contributor · 4 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

The MCP Server module can now send a short block of "instructions" text to every connecting AI client (claude.ai, Claude Code, IDE plugins) as part of the MCP protocol's initialize handshake. Previously the module never populated this field, so clients had no server-level hint about when or how to use the site's exposed tools and resources, only the per-tool descriptions. Site builders can now set this guidance via a new server_instructions configuration value, and other modules can adjust or generate it dynamically.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New server_instructions key in mcp_server.settings, empty by default, surfaced to MCP clients in the initialize handshake when non-empty.
  • New API: New hook_mcp_server_instructions_alter() lets modules set or refine the MCP handshake instructions programmatically.

Technical details

McpServerFactory::build() now calls a new private buildInstructions() helper before constructing the SDK's Server::builder(), and passes the result to setInstructions(). The helper reads server_instructions from mcp_server.settings (added to config/schema/mcp_server.schema.yml and defaulted to an empty string in config/install/mcp_server.settings.yml), then invokes the new hook_mcp_server_instructions_alter() (declared in mcp_server.api.php) via the injected ModuleHandlerInterface, letting other modules override or seed the value, for example to point agents at a companion module's tools. A NULL or empty/whitespace-only result after the hook runs causes the instructions field to be omitted from InitializeResult entirely, matching prior behavior when nothing is configured. The module handler was added as a new constructor dependency on McpServerFactory, wired in mcp_server.services.yml. No admin UI textarea was added for this setting; it's configuration-only for now.

Upgrade

Set the instructions directly in config, or implement the alter hook for dynamic values:

# config/install/mysite.settings.yml or via config import
server_instructions: 'Consult the MCP server before writing code.'

/**
 * Implements hook_mcp_server_instructions_alter().
 */
function mymodule_mcp_server_instructions_alter(?string &$instructions): void {
  if ($instructions === NULL || $instructions === '') {
    $instructions = 'Introspect this Drupal site before writing code.';
  }
}

item.title: #3583079: A denied Explorer execute submission reports an internal exception message and still offers the Execute button
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583079 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

When a user without the right permission tried to execute a tool from the Tool Explorer, the denial page still showed an Execute button, and pressing it produced a second, confusing error exposing an internal developer-facing exception message rather than just the plain access-denied notice. This fix ensures that a denied execution page no longer offers an Execute button, and that submitting a denied (or otherwise un-run) tool reports only the original denial message instead of layering a cryptic internal error on top of it.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was that ToolExecuteForm::buildForm() unconditionally appended the Execute submit button after the plugin form ran, even when the plugin form's access() check had denied execution and returned only denial markup (access_denied). Separately, ToolExecuteForm::submitForm() unconditionally called $tool->getResult() after submission, but ToolBase::getResult() throws a BadMethodCallException if the tool's execute() method never ran, which is exactly the case on a denied submission.

The fix adds two guards in modules/tool_explorer/src/Form/ToolExecuteForm.php: buildForm() now only adds the actions.submit Execute button when $form['access_denied'] is not set, and submitForm() now checks $tool->hasResult() before calling getResult(), returning early (leaving the plugin form's own denial message as the only reported error) when there is no result to retrieve. Kernel test coverage was added in ExecuteToolPluginFormTest (testDeniedPageOffersNoExecuteButton and testDeniedSubmitReportsOnce) to assert the denial page has no submit action and that a denied submission produces exactly one error message with no ::execute() exception text. The issue notes this flaw predates #3583077 (declared-permission pre-checks) but that change made the denial path routine to reach rather than a rare edge case.
